examples.condition: An Ofcom API product listing and rate limit do not prove that a postcode response was retrieved; an authenticated response receipt is required.
Basic and Premium request allowances are capacity planning metadata and must never be stored as broadband availability.
ONSPD assigns boundary-straddling postcodes using the mean grid reference of addresses, so a postcode centroid is not a parcel centroid.
One-metre ONS grid-reference resolution does not authorize nearest-feature or nearest-parcel assignment.
Quarterly ONS releases require snapshot dates to be recorded; a later release must not silently overwrite a pinned join receipt.
BDUK contract management information is not directly comparable with official statistics and cannot replace Ofcom current-r2 coverage.
BDUK figures are rounded to the nearest ten and may not sum, so they cannot support exact row reconciliation.
A variable ingestion lag means BDUK contract tables cannot be used as evidence that a specific build milestone or address is live.
The CO5 Essex and North East England increase of 1,380 built premises is area-level trend context only.
The Essex 9,500-premises expansion announcement describes planned rollout and not current service at the ten target postcodes.
An almost 575,000-premises county footprint cannot be apportioned to RM postcode candidates without an exact address or postcode route.
Local authority Lot 21 and Openreach Type C context must remain separate from product availability and parcel scoring.
